stories.title: UK replaces TCFD climate disclosure rules
stories.summary: The UK Financial Conduct Authority has replaced its TCFD-based climate disclosure requirements with the UK Sustainability Reporting Standards. The regulator adopted a comply or explain approach for both general and climate-related disclosures. Companies must now report on financially material risks or explain why they have not.

stories.title: EU sustainability reporting standards simplified
stories.summary: Simplified EU sustainability reporting standards entered into force Tuesday, cutting mandatory data points by more than 60 percent. The revised rules become mandatory for the 2027 financial year, with reports due in 2028. Companies may choose to apply the standards early for the 2026 reporting cycle.

stories.title: ISSB proposes voluntary nature disclosures
stories.summary: The International Sustainability Standards Board has proposed a framework for companies to disclose how their dependence on natural resources and ecosystems affects financial prospects. The board stopped short of introducing a new standard. Chair Emmanuel Faber noted the disclosures would help investors assess risks to company access.

stories.summary: CRISIL ESG Ratings assigned Equitas Small Finance Bank a score of 68. The rating was issued independently using publicly available information. The bank did not engage CRISIL for the evaluation and did not provide specific data for the process. The score arrived on 9 November.

stories.title: UNCTAD launches global carbon market network
stories.summary: UNCTAD is launching a global network at COP31 to connect fragmented carbon markets and encourage cross-border investment. The initiative aims to improve transparency and market infrastructure. Global carbon pricing generated more than $107 billion in government revenue in 2025, according to the agency.

stories.title: EIB targets 30 billion euro for climate adaptation
stories.summary: The European Investment Bank Group is targeting at least 30 billion euro in global adaptation finance for 2026 to 2030. The plan aims to support climate resilience through new green financing initiatives. The bank is highlighting the importance of moving from commitments to project implementation at COP31.

stories.title: CORSIA credit supply may cover quarter of demand
stories.summary: Credit supply for the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation may cover at most a quarter of demand. Airlines must purchase credits by January 2028 or face penalties. Roland Berger estimates compliance costs between 3.6 billion and 9 billion dollars for the industry.

stories.title: Corporate buyers purchase 2.6 million soil carbon credits
stories.summary: Boomitra has sold 2.6 million soil carbon credits from its Mexico grassland project to corporate buyers. The sales were completed through multiple spot purchases of issued credits. Ranchers and local partners receive at least 75 percent of the gross revenue from the carbon sales.

stories.title: Climate finance pledges drop 70 percent
stories.summary: Public funding pledged to help developing countries tackle climate change has fallen by more than 70 percent in 2026, according to Carbon Brief. Most multi-year pledges expired in 2025. Only five nations have announced new commitments, with the UK being the only major donor among them.

stories.title: Verra approves first CCS carbon credits
stories.summary: Verra has approved the first carbon credits under its carbon capture and storage methodology. The credits originate from a natural gas processing project in Texas that captures carbon dioxide for permanent underground storage. The methodology is designed to support technology-based projects in the voluntary carbon market.

stories.title: Boomitra delivers 2.6 million soil carbon credits
stories.summary: Boomitra has sold and delivered 2.6 million soil carbon credits from a grassland restoration project in Northern Mexico. The company stated these transactions represent completed purchases by corporate buyers rather than future commitments. The revenue will be distributed to local ranching partners involved in the project.

stories.title: UNCTAD to launch carbon market network
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. UNCTAD plans to launch a carbon market network for developing economies at the COP31 summit. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: CIX launches procurement service for carbon credits
stories.summary: Temasek-backed Climate Impact X has launched a centralised procurement service for international carbon credits eligible for offsetting taxable emissions in Singapore. The exchange says the initiative reduces the need for companies to build their own sourcing and settlement capabilities. Supply is expected to become available over time.

stories.title: Albanese omits fossil fuels from COP31 speech
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese told the UN climate summit that governments have a solemn responsibility to act on climate change. He did not mention fossil fuels during his address. Moments earlier, the UN secretary-general stated that keeping the 1.5C temperature goal alive means no new coal.

stories.title: Erdogan labels war in Gaza as ecocide
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan described the war in Gaza as ecocide during his remarks at the COP31 climate summit. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Lula warns of threats to multilateralism
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. Brazilian President Lula stated that science and multilateralism remain under attack while addressing world leaders at the COP31 climate summit in Turkey. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Marshall Islands president warns of climate collapse
stories.summary: Hilda Heine, president of the Marshall Islands, warned leaders at COP31 that failure to respond to the climate crisis means the world as we know it is over. She described the rapid bleaching of coral reefs and the threat of floods destroying schools and hospitals.

stories.title: Egypt calls for affordable climate finance
stories.summary: Egypt's Minister of Local Development and Environment Manal Awad called for affordable climate finance for developing nations at the COP31 leaders summit. Representing President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, she urged the conference to shift its focus from making pledges to the delivery of real implementation.

stories.title: UN chief criticises fossil fuel industry
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres told COP31 attendees that fossil fuels must go the way of the dinosaurs. He noted that while dinosaurs lacked a lobby, the fossil fuel industry possesses one. He reiterated his commitment to speaking on the impact of oil and gas subsidies.

stories.title: UN and EU leaders meet at COP31
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen met on the sidelines of COP31. The leaders discussed cooperation on global challenges, including the situation in Ukraine and the Middle East, alongside the importance of sustained EU leadership on climate change.

stories.title: Guterres calls for end to fossil fuel addiction
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres told COP31 delegates that the case for fossil fuels is collapsing. He urged countries to push for a phase out of energy sources rather than hinting at it. He noted that the industry has a lobby, unlike the dinosaurs.

stories.title: Guterres warns of mutually assured destruction
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned world leaders at COP31 that the climate crisis is outrunning global efforts. He described the current path as one of mutually assured destruction. He urged attendees to fight harder, stating that science is not telling the world to surrender.

stories.title: US, China and India leaders skip COP31
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. Leaders from the United States, China and India are not attending the COP31 climate summit currently taking place in Turkey. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. The United States is not participating in the COP31 climate summit held in Turkey. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Turkish first lady launches zero waste initiative
stories.summary: Turkish first lady Emine Erdogan hosted a high-level meeting of the Global Zero Waste Alliance during the COP31 summit. She stated the alliance represents a commitment to turning shared responsibility into cooperation. The event brought together participants from 195 countries to discuss sustainability goals.

stories.title: World leaders focus on zero waste and methane
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. World leaders at COP31 highlighted zero waste initiatives and pushed for action under the Global Methane Pledge during the third day of the summit.

stories.title: Baling machines market enters phase of structural expansion
stories.summary: The global baling machines market is entering a phase of structural expansion as recycling infrastructure, agricultural mechanization, and industrial waste requirements converge. The market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals and a more regionally diversified supply architecture. Machines now compress materials into dense, transportable bales for global logistics.

stories.title: Circular economy is a national security issue, says minister
stories.summary: Minister Emma Hardy told the ISWA World Congress that transitioning to a circular economy is a national security issue. Hardy argued that failing to recover existing materials leaves the UK exposed to global markets it cannot control. The circular economy is no longer considered a niche technical question.

stories.title: Report calls for policy shake-up to unlock circular economy
stories.summary: The Institution of Mechanical Engineers warns that the UK must reform economic incentives and infrastructure to unlock a circular economy. While engineering solutions exist, the report argues that businesses lack the policy certainty needed to scale them. The transition remains hindered by a persistent take, make, dispose model.

stories.title: Coalition targets 20 percent electrification for international shipping
stories.summary: A coalition of 30 maritime organisations aims to reach 20 percent electrification in international shipping by 2035. The target requires adding two exajoules of annual electricity demand, equivalent to six years of average UK consumption. The initiative was launched at the UN annual climate conference.

stories.title: Amazon launches sustainability accelerator for deep tech
stories.summary: Amazon has announced the Sustainability Deep Tech Accelerator to fast-track low-carbon and circularity technologies. The program aims to validate solutions from materials science and energy firms across the Amazon ecosystem, including AWS and private brands. It intends to create more commercial opportunities for the selected companies.

stories.title: Mercedes-Benz revises climate targets and adds 2049 net zero goal
stories.summary: Mercedes-Benz has dropped its 2039 carbon neutral fleet goal, replacing it with separate targets for production and vehicle use. The company now aims for 90 percent production emission cuts by 2039 and net zero by 2049. Global electric vehicle adoption fell short of the company's original expectations.

stories.title: RWE and KKR secure 17 billion dollar offshore wind financing
stories.summary: RWE and KKR have secured a 17.1 billion dollar financing package for two offshore wind projects in the British North Sea. Backed by 35 international banks, the 2.8 gigawatt development marks the largest project financing in UK offshore wind history. Construction is scheduled to begin next year.

stories.title: Mercedes-Benz signs low-carbon aluminium supply deal
stories.summary: Mercedes-Benz has signed a long-term agreement with Hydro to source low-carbon aluminium, covering 10 percent of its primary needs. The company aims to reduce CO2 emissions to 3kg per kg of aluminium by 2030. The global average currently sits at 14.4kg per kg of aluminium.

stories.title: Iberdrola plans six billion euro grid investment in Spain
stories.summary: Iberdrola plans to double its investment in electricity networks in Spain to six billion euros between 2027 and 2030. It will allocate 1.2 billion euros to the grid in 2027 alone. The company presented the plan to nearly 300 suppliers. The grid is now a group project.

stories.title: Utilities pledge 156 billion dollars for transition infrastructure
stories.summary: Utilities have pledged 156 billion dollars in annual investment for transition infrastructure at COP31. The figure represents the industry commitment to funding the shift toward net zero energy systems. The full piece is for subscribers.
